title: Shopify HubSpot Integration vs Zapier or n8n in 2026
summary: Shopify HubSpot integration connects store data natively through the app, though custom automation requires additional workflow tools.
body_markdown:
## Shopify HubSpot sync errors and fixes


Trace most failures in this pairing and you land on five causes: a stalled first import, contact matching, permissions, API ceilings, and sync direction.


The table lists each symptom with its cause, fix and how well it is documented, so you can tell vendor fact from field folklore.


Symptom Cause from vendor docs Fix Documented or unconfirmed


Duplicate contacts Matching on email only Merge in HubSpot; clean data before connecting Unconfirmed


Missing properties Field not in the app's fixed mapping Add a workflow step for the field Unconfirmed


Reauthorisation Expired or revoked permissions Disconnect, reconnect, accept scopes Unconfirmed


API rate limits Daily request allowance by plan Reduce competing integrations or upgrade Documented (third party)


Sync direction Fixed rules on which side wins Treat Shopify as source of truth Unconfirmed


When a first import sits at a partial count, it is usually still working through history. Check status before reconnecting, because restarting a long import throws away progress.


If properties never arrive, the app's mapping is fixed. A custom Shopify field won't appear, and a workflow tool has to carry it.


When that missing field is the gap, Activepieces can write it for you: a Shopify new-order trigger feeding a HubSpot contact action puts the value into the property the app won't fill.


Its 740 integrations are the entries in the packages/integrations/community directory of the MIT-licensed open source repository on[GitHub](https://www.activepieces.com/pieces/github) , a count anyone can reproduce from the monorepo rather than a figure quoted from a marketing page, and roughly 60% were contributed by the community, so if a connector you need isn't there you can generate one with AI and add it privately to your own instance.


MoneyGram, Moneypenny, Alan and FundingSocieties run it in production.


Duplicates appear when the same person checks out with different emails, or when contacts already exist from forms or imports. Merge them in HubSpot and dedupe your list before you connect.


If sync stops after a staff change, suspect the connecting user's permissions first. Reconnect with an account that can approve every scope. Disconnecting stops new data flowing, but I haven't confirmed what happens to records already synced, so export before you test it.


### HubSpot API rate limits and sync direction


According to[Sam C Barth](https://hubspot.samcbarth.com/articles/hubspot-api-rate-limits/) , Free and Starter accounts get **250,000 API requests per day** . That's a shared pool, so every other connected app draws from it, and a busy store can starve a reporting tool.


Professional gets 625,000, roughly two and a half times as much. Enterprise gets 1,000,000, four times the entry tier.


Direction is the other trap. Since the app's rules are fixed, edits made in HubSpot may not flow back to Shopify, so keep customer data edits in Shopify.
